claim: For the Liu–Du–Zhang–Li–Shi system \(\dot x=ay+xz\), \(\dot y=-bx+yz\), \(\dot z=1-x^2-y^2\), \(\dot w=z(w-1)\) with \(a,b>0\), let \(Q=bx^2+ay^2\). On \(Q>0\), \(I=(w-1)^2/Q\) is an exact first integral and \(w(t)-1=(w(0)-1)\sqrt{Q(t)/Q(0)}\). Every compact ergodic invariant probability measure has support in \(Q>0\), satisfies \(\int z\,d\mu=0\), and has four-dimensional Lyapunov spectrum \(\{\lambda,0,0,-\lambda\}\) for some \(\lambda\ge0\), counting multiplicity. Consequently the exact system has at most one positive Lyapunov exponent on compact recurrent dynamics and cannot be hyperchaotic in the standard two-positive-exponent sense; changes of the initial fourth coordinate with the same \((x,y,z)\) initial condition only rescale the slaved fiber about \(w=1\).

correctness.rationale: For \(Q=bx^2+ay^2\), direct differentiation gives \(\dot Q=2zQ\), while \(u=w-1\) obeys \(\dot u=zu\); hence \(u/\sqrt Q\) and \(u^2/Q\) are exact first integrals on \(Q>0\). Compact invariant supports cannot meet \(Q=0\), because there \(x=y=0\) and \(\dot z=1\). Invariance of \(\log Q\) gives \(\int z\,d\mu=0\). The invariant pure-fiber variational subspace has exponent zero; the base divergence is \(2z\), and its autonomous flow direction has exponent zero, so its remaining exponents are opposite. The packaged symbolic checker verifies every algebraic identity used. No finite-time numerical LE estimate is used as proof.

value.rationale: The source's central novelty claim is a four-dimensional hyperchaotic extension with coexisting hidden attractors. The exact first integral shows that the added coordinate is dynamically slaved, and the spectrum theorem rules out the defining two-positive-exponent feature on compact recurrent dynamics. It also gives a closed-form explanation for projected differences caused solely by changing the fourth initial coordinate. This is a structural correction with direct implications for interpreting the published Lyapunov plots and for validating future simulations or circuit realizations.
